attacks.claim: The plan removes self-hosted sync with no supported replacement. Legacy REST sync ends in app 5.0, the stride-server image is archived, and the Cirrus server is hosted-only. This breaks the README/charter promise to self-host sync and own data for ~3,000 instances, and the removal date is undefined.
attacks.evidence: "Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0 (planned for end of next year), after which Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived." / "the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service"

attacks.claim: Making a proprietary hosted service the sole sync backend creates a one-way door with no exit plan. User data moves to a closed backend the project cannot fork, self-host, or migrate off, and the plan has no fallback if pricing, terms, or availability change.
attacks.evidence: "Adopt Cirrus Sync, a mobile offline-first sync SDK" / "Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend" / ABSENT: any exit or fallback strategy

attacks.claim: A closed-source, commercially licensed binary SDK is bundled into an MIT-licensed open-source app. This is a distribution and license-compatibility risk that the plan does not assess, and it makes the client non-auditable and non-forkable.
attacks.evidence: "distributed as a prebuilt binary (iOS xcframework, Android AAR) under the Cirrus commercial license"

attacks.claim: Downgrade or failed-migration recovery can silently discard 4.0 writes. 3.x restores from stride-backup-v3.db, but the backup is only deleted after 30 days and two syncs, and nothing detects divergence from the Cirrus store or reconciles writes made after migration. The plan also does not show that the Cirrus store can round-trip back to 3.x SQLite format.
attacks.evidence: "If migration fails or the user downgrades to 3.x, 3.x detects stride-backup-v3.db and restores from it" / "the backup is deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs"

attacks.claim: Precise GPS tracks and full workout history move to a third-party processor for ~90k users with no DPA, data residency, sub-processor disclosure, privacy review, or user notice/consent for existing users, including self-hosters, who are migrated.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any DPA, residency, privacy review, or consent/notice step in sections 2, 6, or 7; "Cirrus replicates to Cirrus Cloud when connectivity returns"

attacks.claim: Deletion is incomplete and unverified. The 90-day tombstones, the plaintext stride-backup-v3.db kept up to 30 days, and any legacy-server copies are outside the erasure commitment. The vendor admin API has no stated retry, idempotency, completion verification, or coverage of vendor backups.
attacks.evidence: "Account deletion removes the Cirrus user record and all synced records via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days." / "Deletes are tombstones retained 90 days"

attacks.claim: Authentication and authorization for Cirrus sync are unspecified. The plan does not say how a device identity binds to a user, how records are scoped per account, or where Cirrus admin API credentials live. If deletion runs client-side, embedded admin credentials would be exposed in a distributed binary.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: per-user auth, record ownership, access scoping, or admin credential location; "via the Cirrus admin API"

attacks.claim: The central claim that record-level resumable uploads eliminate partial workouts and duplicates is unproven. No stable record IDs or server-side idempotency are specified, and the only validation is a Week 1 spike that runs after dispatch.
attacks.evidence: "uploads are resumable at the record level, so a dropped connection never leaves a partial workout." / ABSENT: spike results, prototype, or dedupe key

attacks.claim: Conflict semantics are underspecified. Per-field LWW on device hybrid logical clocks has no tie-break or clock-drift bound, so concurrent edits can resolve nondeterministically. The append-only-after-finish rule is not reconciled with concurrent offline writes such as laps or GPS appended after another device's finish.
attacks.evidence: "per-field last-writer-wins using a hybrid logical clock stamped on device" / "Workouts are append-only after the 'finish' event"

attacks.claim: Tombstones expire after 90 days, so a device offline longer than that can resurrect a deleted workout. Nothing detects or prevents this, and the plan does not say how a bad purge would be recovered.
attacks.evidence: "Deletes are tombstones retained 90 days so an offline device cannot resurrect a deleted workout."

attacks.claim: Storage and sync volume are unbounded. Tombstones and change logs have no pruning policy, per-record sync multiplies records per workout, and the migration backup roughly doubles on-device storage for heavy GPS users for 30+ days. No size estimate, batching, or backlog throughput is given.
attacks.evidence: "Per-record change tracking; uploads are resumable at the record level" / "the app copies the existing SQLite database to stride-backup-v3.db" / ABSENT: sizing, pruning, or throughput

attacks.claim: The cost case rests on a single assertion. The plan gives no budget for Cirrus usage or hosting, no growth projection against the 100k device cap, no overage ceiling, and no contingency for pricing changes. The free-tier fit is also unsourced.
attacks.evidence: "Pricing: free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier." / ABSENT: pricing source, growth projection, or cost ceiling

attacks.claim: The rollout has no data-integrity halt criterion, and the success metric relies on client-reported sync success, which is least reliable in the offline and partial-failure cases this rewrite targets. Halting on crash-free rate does not detect or reverse silent data loss or duplication.
attacks.evidence: "halting if crash-free sessions drop below 99.3%" / "Sync success rate (client-reported) >= 99.5% on beta cohort."

attacks.claim: The 5-week, 3-contributor build bundles an SDK adoption, a sync-engine replacement, a multi-table data migration, a server hosting change, and a protocol sunset. That is not a reviewable or credible scope for this timeline, and there is no slack.
attacks.evidence: "Week 1: Cirrus integration spike" through "Week 5: staged rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100%"

attacks.claim: App data model, sync transport, and conflict rules are coupled to a closed SDK and a hosted-only backend. The plan defines no abstraction boundary, so LWW and tombstone logic cannot be unit-tested without the vendor binary.
attacks.evidence: "Local writes go to an on-device Cirrus store" / "Unit tests cover the 14 conflict scenarios" with no abstraction layer described

attacks.claim: The migration backup is a plaintext copy of the full workout database, including GPS and health-adjacent data, left on device for up to 30 days, with no encryption or file-protection note.
attacks.evidence: "the app copies the existing SQLite database to stride-backup-v3.db"

attacks.claim: Client-reported sync telemetry from the beta, which includes GPS-linked trail-run logs, has no stated minimization, retention, or consent.
The 23% issue-share figure has no stated query, denominator, or labelling method, so the problem magnitude and the 80% target rest on unverified numbers.
attacks.evidence: "23% of sync-related GitHub issues in the last 6 months" / ABSENT: query or method

attacks.claim: Test coverage relies on an external document whose contents and existence are not confirmed in the artifact.
attacks.evidence: "Unit tests cover the 14 conflict scenarios enumerated in docs/sync-conflicts.md."
